whyItMatters: Making the EKS Kubernetes API endpoint publicly reachable expands the cluster's external attack surface.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker or administrator can create or reconfigure an EKS cluster so the API server is internet reachable by setting resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess=true or by broadening publicAccessCidrs.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: Publicly reachable Kubernetes control planes are a recurring misconfiguration class in cloud security assessments and post-compromise attack paths.
threatContext.whyItMatters: This is a meaningful exposure-change event, especially when the cluster was previously private-only or restricted to narrow CIDRs.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If this goes unnoticed, internet-originated access attempts against the cluster API become possible, and any later identity compromise has a much easier path to exploitation.

loggingRequirements: CloudTrail must capture EKS management events.
Detection should evaluate both CreateCluster and UpdateClusterConfig.
For widening logic, retain prior cluster endpoint configuration or enrich from DescribeCluster.
limitations: A CreateCluster request may omit endpointPublicAccess while the service default remains public.
Detecting CIDR widening accurately requires comparison against prior state.
Public endpoint exposure is not the same as anonymous access.

rawToNormalized.notes: Allowed source CIDRs for the public endpoint

enrichment.description: Add the sensitivity and operational importance of the cluster.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Keeps dev/test exposure changes from looking as urgent as production platform changes.

enrichment.description: Compare the new endpoint settings with prior state and with the cluster's private access posture.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Distinguishes harmless narrowing changes from true internet exposure or widening.

enrichment.description: Identify whether the update came from infrastructure automation or an ad hoc operator session.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Known IaC-driven endpoint updates are less suspicious than manual console or CLI changes.

enrichment.description: Profile the actor authorized to change EKS networking and cluster access settings.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Endpoint exposure by a non-platform actor is much higher signal than the same change by a trusted cluster admin.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should focus on explicit EKS API exposure changes rather than a broad CreateCluster or UpdateClusterConfig baseline. The strongest stateless matches are endpointPublicAccess=true and publicAccessCidrs including 0.0.0.0/0 or another obviously broad CIDR.
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Treat 0.0.0.0/0 as higher severity than a narrow corporate CIDR range. 2. Enrich with prior endpoint state so you can suppress narrowing changes. 3. Downgrade approved dev clusters while keeping prod and shared platform clusters high severity.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire on any explicit public endpoint enablement and on clearly broad public CIDR exposure.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Medium (legitimate dev and migration use cases exist, especially without state comparison)
quality.expectedVolume: Low in mature environments, but can spike during cluster migration or networking changes

deployment.scheduling: Real-time on CloudTrail management events is practical; a scheduled batch rule every 5 to 15 minutes is also sufficient.
considerations: Use CloudTrail for change detection and DescribeCluster or config snapshots for prior-state comparison.
This is best treated as an exposure-change rule, not as proof of successful unauthorized Kubernetes access.
